title: Cross-environment Privilege Delegation and Evidence Routing
content:
Purpose:
This working doc lays out an operationally grounded design for delegating privileges across Redwood's three hosting tiers (hosted / dedicated / private), plus a companion SIEM export and evidence-routing scheme to support automated audits and attestation. The goal is to reduce manual evidence collection, enable fast incident investigation, and keep tenant isolation guarantees intact while enabling legitimate cross-boundary operations (support, oncall, migrations).

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to RBAC v2 concepts (role, scope, bindings, ephemeral grants) used by control plane and tenant-plane components.
- Excludes application-level feature flags; focuses on access to infrastructure, customer data access surfaces, and admin tooling.
- Must preserve least-privilege by default and ensure every delegated action produces tamper-evident telemetry exported to a SIEM pipeline with evidence links.

High-level design summary:
1) Roles and delegation principals:
   - Primary role classes: Viewer, Operator, TenantAdmin, SupportAgent, InfraAdmin, AuditReader, IncidentResponder.
   - Distinguish two principal types: human (user) and machine (service account).
   - All elevated grants must be ephemeral and minted via an authorization broker (short-lived token). No long-lived impersonation.

2) Scopes and scoping hierarchy:
   - Global (organization): cluster-wide infra controls, billing, security config.
   - Region: region-limited resource groups (cloud region, physical DC).
   - Tenant: customer-scoped resources (models, keys, datasets).
   - Node/Instance: lowest-level compute resource (used for SRE troubleshooting with guardrails).

3) Delegation patterns supported:
   - Cross-tier support delegation: SupportAgent in hosted can request scoped read-only tokens for a tenant in Dedicated if the customer has opted-in (explicit contract).
   - Emergency breakglass: timeboxed InfraAdmin elevation available via ticket and two-person approval; fully auditable and auto-revoked.
   - Service account temporary elevation: CI/CD may request elevated perms for migrations; requires signed runbook and audit hook.

Role matrix (textual):
- Viewer: Org->no, Region->read, Tenant->read, Node->no. Purpose: read-only dashboards and billing.
- Operator: Org->no, Region->operator, Tenant->support-read, Node->ssh-no (not allowed). Purpose: routine ops.
- TenantAdmin: Org->no, Region->no, Tenant->full, Node->no. Purpose: tenant self-admin.
- SupportAgent: Org->no, Region->no, Tenant->support-read/limited-write (with acceptance), Node->no. Purpose: assist tenants with opt-in.
- InfraAdmin: Org->full, Region->full, Tenant->no (unless explicitly delegated), Node->full. Purpose: platform maintenance.
- IncidentResponder: Org->read, Region->read-write (incidents), Tenant->audit-read, Node->diagnostic-only.
- AuditReader: Org->read, Region->read, Tenant->read, Node->no. Purpose: compliance audits.

Environment-specific rules (hosted / dedicated / private):
- Hosted (multi-tenant managed): Default: no cross-tenant read access. SupportAgent access requires tenant opt-in flag and recorded consent. All actions produce an audit event with tenant_id and consent_token. SIEM export: high-fidelity telemetry retained for 365 days (configurable). KMS keys are platform-managed (no tenant-key access to Redwood employees).
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated infra): Tenant data isolated. Platform maintainers have ability to perform cloud-provider level remediation via separate support workflow with dual-approval and recorded evidence. Privilege delegation requires customer pre-approval; emergency breakglass allowed with customer notification and automatic forensics snapshot export. SIEM export includes resource mapping to customer project/account.
- Private (on-prem / VPC): Redwood control-plane minimal by default. Customer-managed control plane may host audit logs. For evidence automation, we require a signed collector contract (agent config) and explicit log export endpoints. If Redwood needs access, it must be via customer-issued ephemeral creds and documented ROA.

Audit log schema (core fields):
- timestamp_iso8601 (string): event time in UTC.
- event_id (string): UUID v4.
- principal_type (string): user | service_account | external_operator.
- principal_id (string): internal user id or service account id.
- principal_display (string): human-friendly name/email.
- action (string): canonical action id (e.g., tenant.read.object, infra.node.reboot).
- resource_type (string): tenant | model | instance | k8s_pod | kms_key.
- resource_id (string): canonical resource identifier (tenant:<id> or arn-like strings).
- scope_level (string): org | region | tenant | node.
- outcome (string): success | denied | error.
- auth_method (string): password | oauth | mfa | brokered-ephemeral | signed-runbook.
- justification_id (string): id of the ticket/runbook used for the grant (if any).
- request_trace (string): tracing id linking to request path.
- evidence_links (list): list of signed-urls to artefacts (forensics, screenshots, k8s logs).
- tenant_consent_token (string): present if action touches tenant data and was consented.
- retention_policy_tag (string): e.g., default365, sensitive730, PII_10yrs.
- siem_severity (string): mapped severity (low|medium|high|critical).

Note: the above is deliberately compact to ensure mapping to most SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo, Elastic). Fields expected by SOC playbooks are highlighted: event_id, principal_id, action, resource_id, outcome, request_trace.

SIEM export mapping and enrichment rules:
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON events pushed to an index named redwood_audit_{env} or forwarded via Kafka topic 'audit-events' with schema version header.
- Enrichment at export: append geoip based on request_source_ip, map ldap_group to role_name via cached mapping, and add 'evidence_bucket' pointer where artefacts will be deposited.
- Alert rules to surface: repeated denied privileged actions (threshold 5 in 10m), breakglass activations without corresponding ticket, service-account elevation without signed runbook.

Evidence automation flow (playbook):
1) Trigger: privileged action or emergency workflow initiates.
2) Collector: ephemeral forensic collector spins up (read-only snapshots, system journal export, container logs, and relevant KV cache dumps).
3) Packaging: collector signs bundle (sha256) and uploads to evidence store (S3 with immutability/TLP tags).
4) Link emission: audit event includes evidence_links pointing to signed pre-signed URLs plus manifest id.
5) Retention & attestation: retention_policy_tag applied; attestation record created and emailed to compliance owners for large-impact events (critical severity).

Sample policy template (human-friendly pseudo-YAML, replace tokens before use):
- policy_name: support-tenant-read-opt-in
  description: 'Grant read-only support access to tenant resources when customer opt-in is true.'
  conditions:
    - tenant.opt_in == true
    - principal.role == SupportAgent
    - auth_method == brokered-ephemeral
  allowed_actions:
    - tenant.read.*
  denied_actions:
    - tenant.write.*
  audit: true
  evidence_capture: 'automatic'
  siem_severity: low

Sample breakglass flow (steps to implement):
- Request via ticketing system, link ticket to justification_id.
- Two approvers from different org units sign.
- Authorization broker mints ephemeral token (max 4 hours).
- Automatic forensic snapshot launched; evidence_links attached.
- Post-incident required: detailed runbook and attestation within 72 hours.

Operational checks and automation suggestions:
- Enforce token durations in the authorization broker and deny refresh for breakglass tokens.
- Periodic (weekly) automated scans for stale role bindings > 30 days without activity. Report bindings to owners and auto-expire if no owner.
- SIEM export must include both raw events and an enriched "investigation view" index where the evidence manifest is pre-joined to speed triage.
- Implement a read-only sandbox where security can replay events using the request_trace id without touching production data.

Open questions / decisions needed (working list):
- Customer consent UX: how explicit must opt-in be for hosted multi-tenant support? checkbox vs contract clause? (Product / Legal)
- Retention windows: default365 covers majority, but PII-heavy customers will require longer; how to surface extra-cost retention tiers? (Finance / Sales)
- Collector footprint: what are the safe minimal artefacts we snapshot in Private environments where customers worry about data exfil? (Security / SRE)

Immediate next steps (owners assigned):
- Priya Kapoor: draft the authorization-broker API spec and TTL enforcement (due 2026-03-24).
- Owen Hart: prototype SIEM export topic + enrichment lambda and publish example parquet sink (due 2026-04-01).
- Marisol Jimenez: finalize audit schema JSON schema and run a compatibility test with Splunk ingest (due 2026-03-20).

Appendix A — quick checklist for oncall engineers before executing cross-tenant operations:
- Confirm tenant opt-in or signed customer approval.
- Link ticket to justification_id and attach runbook.
- Verify authorization broker issued ephemeral token and that token TTL is set.
- Confirm evidence collector is enabled and evidence_links are returned.
- Notify compliance if the action is high or critical.

Appendix B — example SIEM event (newline-delimited JSON example, single-line):
{
  "timestamp_iso8601": "2026-03-10T15:12:01Z",
  "event_id": "6f7a9f66-1d4b-4c2b-8a8b-2f0d3ea7c8d9",
  "principal_type": "user",
  "principal_id": "u-03457",
  "principal_display": "support+east@redwood.ai",
  "action": "tenant.read.model_config",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "resource_id": "tenant:acme:models:m-42",
  "scope_level": "tenant",
  "outcome": "success",
  "auth_method": "brokered-ephemeral",
  "justification_id": "TICKET-4512",
  "request_trace": "trace-0a1b2c3d",
  "evidence_links": ["https://evidence.redwood.internal/signed/manifest-1234"],

Document history: initial draft and working notes. This doc should be iterated with Product, Legal, and SRE before being promoted to a final playbook.
